item.title: After The Quake
item.description:
A short collection of stories by Haruki Murakami written around a big earthquake that destroys Tokyo. In all the stories characters struggle through their regular life problems and emotional issues, where the tides turn when the earthquake hit the city. Despite the tragic situation, Murakami managed to keep characters positive with thoughtful endings.

There is also a story, the best one in my view, where a frog tries to convince a lonely hard-working man that his morals are important to save the world from earthquake, but ending is surprising. So to know the ending, I encourage you to read the book. It's a short one (less than 200 pages), and I finished it in around two hours by listening it on self-hosted Kokoro text to voice agent.

Despite the positives, the break in story made the book a bit boring, so I wont pick up again second time. I can only give it 3 stars.

item.title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
item.description:
Imagine a story where a young couple who are distant cousins wants to get married but the family warns them that if they do it, their offspring will be born with a pig's tail and die a horrible death. They both become worry but in the end, you can guess, they did not take the superstitious warning seriously and along with friends move to a distant place where they build a small village, Macondo. In following years, they (Buendia family) have three children and none of them is born with a pig's tail. They live happily, for first twenty years in which many people from far land including gypsies regularly visit Macondo. However, after those peaceful years, the remote Macondo start seeing a wave of globalization where government tries to control it. The political turmoil erupts and goes on for next eighty years during which seven generations pass and Macondo sees its first telegraph, train, industry and war. Although most of the story looks trivial, the regular visits of dead people, premonitions, invisibility and time running in a loop give it a touch for which this book is known. It is impossible to predict what will happen next, and the ending leaves reader in awe and fear. This might be the reason that the book won 1982 Nobel Prize in literature.

The book is moderate in size and quite addictive, at least for first half. There is a significant change in second half where many new characters emerge for a brief period. Reading them was quite boring. However, the overall story telling is neat, less cluttered with details, and has a poetic touch. This is the core strength of the book where author describes mundane things in such a beautiful manner that the lines stay with the reader. One example is:

One night he sang. Macondo woke up in a kind of angelic stupor that was caused by a zither that deserved more than this world and a voice that led one to believe that no other person on earth could feel such love. Pietro Crespi then saw the lights go on in every window in town except that of Amaranta.

Even though due to ADHD I usually struggle with fiction, this book was an easy read. It has a deeper impact on me, especially the tragedies revolving around the Buendia family. I highly recommend it. 5 stars

item.title: What I Talk About When I Talk About Running
item.description:
This is a memoir of Haruki Murakami, I mentioned about in the previous book post. Here the author describes his journey of becoming a novelist from a bar owner and how sport activities, especially running, helped him in doing so. He became a serious long distance runner in his early thirties while prior to that time he was rarely active. So reading his journey was inspiring. The author revealed many nuances for amateur runners that can be helpful in developing long-distance running habit—at least it was helpful for me. For instance:

The main thing was not the speed or distance so much as running every day, without taking a break.

It is a short book so one can finish it in a single read. However, I took it slow because I did not want this book to end. Reading it inspired me and gave me a new understanding of long-distance running. I highly recommend it with 4 stars.

item.title: Hear the Wind Sing
item.description:
This is the second book of Murakami I am reading, which I finished before finishing the first one. I was impressed by his writing style while reading his memoir where he mentioned about this book. So I decided to check his first creation as a writer.

It's a short book without any concrete story. The protagonist discusses mundane events of his daily life, such as meeting with friends and dating girls. So overall it is a bit boring. However, whats amazing is that it showed how Murakami build himself from this writing style to what he is known for. That's why I have read it.

So you can read it if you are free and looking for passing time. I recommend it with 3 stars.

item.title: The Green Mile
item.description:
This movie is impressive due to two reasons: first one is the storytelling in a nostalgic manner with a balanced approach to magic realism. The second one is a strong star cast, especially Tom Hanks. His acting is always fascinating due to his ability to deal with complex scenes, with hard emotions. I have seen a very few actors who can do that.

The story revolves around the protagonist, Paul Edgecomb, the head of a prison, who witnesses healing powers of a falsely acquitted African man. He learns from his first hand experiences that the African man is innocent but he can not do anything. It is a complicated situation where he is bound to do his duty while it is also wrong to swing the death sentence of an innocent man with divine powers. This dilemma leads to situations which has deep impact on you (the viewer), and for which you should watch the movie.

I loved every minute of the movie. Highly recommend it. 5 stars.

item.title: Ghost Dog: The Way of the Samurai (1999)
item.description:
A weird crime cinema, at least for modern times, amalgamating criminal mind with Samurai code. That's exactly the theme of the movie.

A professional killer, alias Ghost Dog, strictly follows Samurai code. He is a big fan of Japanese culture, and an avid reader who repeatedly quote many times from a book Hagakure—a practical and spiritual guide for a warrior written in nineteenth century—throughout the movie.

The story line is simple, a killer eliminating people who want to kill him, and yet it leaves a deep impact. I think one need to watch it again to understand it properly. I recommend it with 4 stars.`

item.title: A Thousand Splendid Suns
item.description:
Just finished this book yesterday, and the words I have to describe the book are tragedy, tragedy, and tragedy. This book kept me at the edge from beginning to end. I was anxious while reading every single page, fearing that something bad would happen. So for sure, it is not a book for lighthearted people or for those who have some past trauma.

The story is set in Soviet-era Kabul, Afghanistan up to the time when US army came to fight Taliban. There is no single protagonist in this book, but in a web of characters the focus is on two women, Mariam and Laila, whose fates are bound together through many tragic changes in life, and Afghanistan. When Soviets left the country, the political ground shifted and Afghani warlords took over, bombing houses, hospitals, schools, and almost everything. Freedom was gone, especially for women, food became scarce, and no one was safe. Everyone hoped for a miracle, and one seemed to rise in the refugee camps of Pakistan, the Taliban.

Sadly, when Taliban took over, the situation became worse. They imposed strong sharia laws where reciting poetry, singing songs and studying science all were sinful. The government even forbade to show a flamingo bird without pajamas because showing its naked leg was a sin. Now imagine the situation of women that time. There was a lot of violence against everyone. The way Hosseini described it will make your heart sink.

It's a classic Hosseini style, I guess, to write every scene in a tragic way. This made me feel both anxious and scared. I wanted to run away from the book but also to finish the story. I understand that he tried to describe the real situation of Afghanistan to make people aware of real struggle of Afghans in war, and not just how it looked on American televisions. And he succeeded in his goal.

The ending of the book is beautiful and left me in tears and rumination. So for those bold heart people, I recommend it with 4 stars.

item.title: WV17-A writing struggle
item.description:
This post is a part of my word-vomit series. Feel free to skip it.

I have not written any long post for almost a month as I felt my writing juices were over. I needed to replenish them to start writing but I guess that will take a long time. Meanwhile, I was posting about books and movies, both of which I am consuming a lot nowadays. Even in these posts, I was either feeling that I have not much to write or the topics are not important. Although, I had occasional motivation to write about different topics such as habits, some skills, and running, for an ADHD mind like mine these bursts did not last long. The moment passed so did the energy of writing. It's a pity as at that time I felt those topics were important but once I forgot them, I did not feel their importance that strongly.

It is an irony to write about not writing again and again, repeating myself countless times here, here, and here. A serious reader would not like it. But do I even have a serious reader? (Sorry for you, if you exist).

Dear reader, I guarantee that it is not intentional. I feel that I have important things to say, especially due to my sharp observant nature. But writing them takes time, and after a day I have plethora of new observations and new ideas. The situation is overwhelming when I am not delivering enough but have more ideas, and higher expectations.

Now you might be expecting that finally I will say something wise or entertaining. Nope. I will not. I want to run away in shame, hide my face under the pillow. Like Mariam did when her husband Rashid tried to hit her with leather belt and Laila (the second wife) hold it and snatched it to prevent the violence. Mariam was scared; so am I. That was from a book I am reading, A Thousand Splendid Suns by Khaled Hosseini.

Regardless of me being wise or boring, I want to tell you about one of my recent happy moments. I was using Obsidian for quite some time but a few weeks ago it started throwing error on launch. Using Claude, I understood it was a plugin overload. But I was only using 4-5 community plugins. So I was fed up. I decided to quit Obsidian and make my own writing software where I can save my drafts as well. The best candidate for it was my micro-publishing client. I just needed to work on its writing section. So now I have this amazing personalized writing page where I can write and save the drafts. So cool. I am happy writing this post in my micropub client. This strategy also has reduced the number of steps I need to publish. Often, the draft in Obsidian stays there and gets abandoned. But here I feel motivated to finish a piece of text, otherwise it will be sitting on my a**, forever.

A side note. My AI usage is growing, and I am okay with it. I mostly use it for writing new codes and developing tools which would have taken me months if done without AI.

Time to go now. See you next time.

item.title: The Last Wish: Introducing the Witcher (1999)
item.description:
If you have read my review (comments) of the TV series The Witcher, you know my disappointment for Henry Cavill leaving after third season. Following that I decided to read the original source (this book) so that I can see the real Witcher from the book. And may be it will help me feel a bit better.

The series follow the story of a half human half magical-being Geralt of Rivia who is also known as The Witcher. He used to be a human as a little child but he was abducted and converted to a Witcher. So it is a type of being in this magical universe, along with Sorcerers, Demons, Djinns, Elfs and so on. This book is the first in the series where the author introduce The Witcher universe.

I am not a fan of this genre (due to my short attention span, ADHD) but I was overall happy with the book. It took me some time (may be 3-4 months) to finish but whenever I was reading it I was enjoying it. Author kept it nicely balanced between scenery details and pace of the story. By not giving superfluous amount of scenery details, he made it ADHD friendly :)

I am unsure whether I will be reading next book in the series any time soon but I look forward to it.

I recommend it with 4 stars.

item.title: Interpreter of Maladies (1999)
item.description:
This book is a collection of nine short stories written by Indian American author Jhumpa Lahiri, exploring the life of migrated Indian families in USA. These stories give you a window to see in the life of Indian families living in America, especially the cultural shock, loneliness, and their struggle to adopt the American life.

A daily life of immigrant might be boring for most people but when you move thousands of kilometers far from home country (unwillingly, just to survive) and whole world see your culture as an alien one then it matters. Thats what I liked about the book as it tries to capture this alien-ness Indian people feel in different countries, especially during 60-70s time. Now situation is bit better as we have advance communication technology.

The author won Pulitzer prize for the book. However, out of nine stories at least two tested my patience. Those were felt prolonged without any major conclusion. I wont reveal their name to not to spoil other's experience.

I recommend it reading at least once. So 3 stars.
